title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction thresholds and spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncontrolled spillover to host memory have been the primary drivers of token latency regressions under mixed-workload scenarios. This PR implements adaptive eviction thresholds, improved spillover paging heuristics, and a lightweight compaction signal to reduce fragmentation and page churn while preserving cache hit rate.

Summary of changes: 
- Introduce adaptive eviction thresholds per-slab based on live fragmentation and recent access density. Thresholds scale between 60%-95% of slab capacity (configurable).
- New spillover paging policy: prefer coalesced pages (recently-accessed contiguous keys) and delay low-benefit spillover during brief load spikes.
- Add compaction hint: background compaction is triggered when fragmentation > 30% and net active entries < 75% of slab capacity for 60s. Compaction runs are rate-limited and piggyback on existing scheduler slots.
- Tune continuous batching interaction: batching window now honors a small holdback when compaction is active to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Expose control-plane knobs: rv.eviction.adaptive_enabled, rv.eviction.min_threshold, rv.eviction.max_threshold, rv.spillover.coalesce_window_ms, rv.compaction.enabled, rv.compaction.fragmentation_trigger_pct.

Design notes: 
- The adaptive threshold uses an EWMA of per-slab fragmentation and access density; more fragmented slabs receive lower retention thresholds to encourage selective eviction. We avoid global thresholds to prevent cache thrashing across heterogeneous workloads.
- Spillover policy attempts to write contiguous KV segments to host pages; it batches spill writes and introduces a small spill_delay_ms if incoming request rate exceeds thresholds to amortize writes.
- Compaction is best-effort and cooperative: it yields to inference-critical tasks and runs at low priority. We ensure compaction cannot block request fast-paths.

Testing and benchmarks: 
- Unit tests for eviction threshold updates, spill coalesce behavior, and compaction trigger logic.
- Integration perf harness runs on perf-canary with mixed chat/long-context workloads (median seq 1024, 1% tail 4096) show: 6-12% reduction in 95th percentile token latency under high fragmentation scenarios and 8% decrease in host memory spill throughput.
- Regression checks: average token latency unchanged (<1%) for low-fragmentation steady-state workloads.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation (runtime + control-plane knobs)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf benchmarks and baseline comparisons in perf-canary
- [x] Documentation for control-plane flags
- [x] Feature-gated and off by default (rv.eviction.adaptive_enabled=false)

Related: Linear ENG-1427, ENG-2131. Closes INVEST-112 (kv-cache perf incident).

review_thread: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach, I like per-slab thresholds. Two asks: add docstring for EWMA window and ensure we have a safe default for tiny slabs.
Aisha Kumar: Thanks — added docstring and tiny-slab clamp (min 4 entries) in the latest commit.
Diego Martinez: Can compaction starve inference under pathological conditions? Need a hard CPU/MS cap on compaction.
Aisha Kumar: Compaction now respects schedulerQuota and a max_cpu_pct config (default 5%). Added test to verify it yields to fast-path.
Xiao Li: Perf numbers look good. Please add an operator note about enabling feature in Dedicated clusters with low host-memory budgets.
Aisha Kumar: Added docs/operator/kv-cache-eviction.md with recommended defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management by adding adaptive eviction thresholds, spillover coalescing, and background compaction heuristics. Reduces tail token latency and host spill throughput in fragmented workloads. Feature gated off by default.
notes: Feature is behind control-plane flag and rollout will be gradual (canary -> staged -> all). Ops alerted and default disabled.
